items.stem: Raghavan shows that two triangles are congruent using the steps below. AC = FG CD = GH ∠C = ∠G Thus, ∆ACD ≅ ∆FGH Which criterion was used by Raghavan to prove the congruence of the two triangles?
Two triangles are congruent when their three corresponding sides are of equal measure. Is it the same when the three corresponding angles are equal? Give reasons.
items.answer: No, with valid reasoning. | No, two triangles are not said to be congruent if all three angles of one triangle are congruent to corresponding angles of another because they may not superimpose each other. | No, two triangles are not said to be congruent if all three angles of one triangle are congruent to corresponding angles of another because they may have different side length.
